hardRules: Only edit or add test files.
Every new test must pass against the original production code.
Every new test must fail against the listed mutant behavior.
Do not delete, skip, or mark existing tests as todo.
Do not write filler tests such as expect(true).toBe(true).
If you find a real production bug, stop and report it instead of silently rewriting implementation.
validationLoop: Run the normal test suite against the original production code.
Use tautest verify --from <original-report> --mutant <id> --test <candidate-file> to verify each target; add --file if ids repeat.
Require a verified result: the initial suite passed and an executed test in the selected file killed the exact mutant.
If the target survives, the run fails or the budget expires, do not claim a verified fix.
Refresh the full report with the existing Stryker command and analyze it again.
commands: # Use tautest verify with the original report, mutant id and candidate test file.

insight.missingBehavior: The exact boundary value 18 may not be protected by a test that distinguishes the original expression from the mutant. Confirm the two sides actually produce different results before treating this as a gap.
insight.whyThisMatters: A comparison boundary can move by one value while existing tests still pass, but some boundary shifts (for example a redundant guard) never change the observable result and are equivalent mutants rather than gaps.
insight.suggestedTestIdea: If 18 and its neighbor produce different observable results, add a boundary test for the exact value 18. If they behave the same either way, this is likely an equivalent mutant; consider a documented Stryker ignore instead of writing a test.
